title: Implement color theming logic (Stage 6 — brand-derived or palette-mapped)
description: Implement src/lib/ai/theming.ts which selects or derives the color palette for a site. If branding was extracted from the crawl, derives a full palette from the brand colors. If no branding, maps the AI's palette hint (from the structure decision) to the closest pre-built palette.
acceptanceCriteria: Returns a `{ paletteId: string, customPalette?: Record<string, string> }` object
If branding.colors has entries: derives a full 22-token palette using the primary brand color
If no branding colors: maps paletteHint string to the closest pre-built palette by name matching
Derived palettes have correct hover, light, dark variants calculated from primary color
Returns a valid palette in all cases (never undefined)

steps.details: Import palette utilities from `src/lib/palettes.ts`. Define the function signature: `selectPalette(branding: BrandingData, paletteHint: string): { paletteId: string, customPalette?: Record<string, string> }`.

When no brand colors: compare `paletteHint.toLowerCase()` against palette names and IDs. Simple substring matching: if 'blue' in hint, try 'ocean-blue'. If 'green', try 'forest-green', etc. Fallback: return the first available palette. Return `{ paletteId: matchedId }`.

When brand colors exist: take the most prominent brand color (first in the array). Use it as `--color-primary`. Derive:
- primary-hover: darken by 10% (subtract ~20 from each RGB channel)
- primary-light: lighten to 90% luminosity (mix 90% white)
- primary-dark: darken by 20%
- accent: use second brand color if available, else amber fallback
All other tokens (background, surfaces, text) use sensible light-theme defaults. Return `{ paletteId: 'custom', customPalette: derivedTokens }`.

Call with `branding = { colors: ['#c41e3a', '#ffffff', '#1a1a2e'] }` (red/white/dark site). Verify the derived palette has a red primary, appropriate lighter/darker variants, and readable text colors.

technicalNotes: Color math: to darken a hex color by N%, parse to RGB, multiply each channel by (1 - N/100), convert back to hex.
To lighten: mix with white: `channel = channel + (255 - channel) * (N/100)`.
Ensure text contrast: if derived primary is very dark, use white text-inverted; if very light, use dark text-inverted.
The derived palette is stored in the `custom_palette` JSON field on the prospect record.
